bullets: CRL 2026 broadcast game vs "Surgical Goblin" on Log Bait (video 637.6-926.6s; the broadcast overlay hides the match clock, so all citations are video seconds). Ryley: "I had this Goblin Drill deck, and this was the first time in the entire tournament that I actually whipped out Goblin Drill" (636-642s).

The deck's whole plan against bait is small-spell coverage plus corner drills: "normally log bait does lose to Goblin Drill Snowball or Goblin Drill normally loses to Log Bait, right? With the snowball and the poison, I knew that I could still win this matchup if I played well" (665-676s).

All seven Goblin Drills go to the enemy left corner at (2, 22)-(2, 24) (t=645, 713.7, 765.8, 817.8, 820.8, 839.8, 872.9, 887.9, 890.9); the enemy left tower drops 2085 -> 1096 between 816s and 894s purely on that chip while he defends everything else.

Defence is a repeating Cannon + Fire Spirit + Giant Snowball + Bomber package, with Knight and Berserker as bodies — "get a cannon plus uh fire spirit snowball on defense" (869-871s), "I went for the fire spirit bomber here and then just cannon on defense, making sure to get those wall breakers off the board" (773-778s).

At ~2.6 average elixir the deck wins by out-cycling the bait deck, and Ryley says that explicitly: "Dude, I was dropping my cards so quickly in this game... I was getting the cards down so quickly to not get out cycled by this deck" (873-879s).

Poison is spent on the Magic Archer at a knowing loss rather than saved for value — "I'm okay with going down, you know, one even to three elixir sometimes just to make it so I don't have to like worry about it at the bridge" (800-807s).

The Knight is the Hero variant; the 2-elixir Triumphant Taunt shows up at t=756.8 ("here I went for the knight ability") and as a misclick at t=821.7 ("I clicked on my knight"). The evolution slot held the Goblin Drill, not the Cannon, which he says changes the game plan: "Evo drill does allow me to be a lot more aggressive... Whereas the Evo cannon, I just have to play really, really good defense" (717-724s).

The clip is cut before the result screen; the commentary at 928s ("But guys, I was able to take game number...") is the only evidence of the win. Final readable towers at 926.6s: own 1698 / 1232, enemy 964 / 1845.

new_deck.rationale: Eight cards averaging ~2.6 elixir with no tank and a single cheap chip win condition, played by out-cycling the opponent and answering every push with 1-3 elixir defenders.
new_deck.why_it_works_md: The deck has one win condition — Goblin Drill in the enemy corner — and seven cards whose job is to survive the cycle. Cannon, Fire Spirit, Bomber, Berserker and Knight cover almost every ground push for two or three elixir, so the drill chip accumulates faster than the opponent's does. Giant Snowball and Poison are chosen specifically for the bait matchup: Snowball handles Goblin Barrel and Wall Breakers on his own half, Poison answers a deep Magic Archer and adds to the drill's damage on the far tower. Ryley's own framing is that this pair flips a matchup that normally goes the other way — "normally log bait does lose to Goblin Drill Snowball or Goblin Drill normally loses to Log Bait" — but only if the pilot keeps cycling fast enough not to be out-cycled, and accepts negative spell trades to keep the Magic Archer off the bridge.
